rationale: Both are clean data-driven solutions with the same recite loop and a spider-suffix special case. A keys the comments by animal name and tests special verses by name (animal == "horse", animal != "fly"), which makes the intent self-evident. B keys the comments by integers 1-8, which merely duplicates list positions; a list or name-keyed dict would be clearer. B also checks the magic numbers verse == 8 and verse > 1, and builds the chain by reassigning the animal variable inside the loop, which is a little less obvious. B does have nice touches, a module docstring and a named _SPIDER_TAIL constant. A's reversed(list(zip(...))) line is dense and overly long, but on balance A's semantic naming and lack of magic numbers make it slightly better.
